newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand plans to issue zero-coupon bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thailand plans to issue zero-coupon bonds.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Friday that his ministry planned to issue zero-coupon bonds to raise funds for use in assisting the ailing finance and property sectors.

His statement followed newspaper reports on Friday that the ministry planned to issue the bonds after a major shake up of the troubled finance sector. He said all details pertaining to the bonds were being discussed now.
Amnuay said the bonds would be sold at a discount and holders of the bonds would not be paid interest but would make capital gains when they sold them.
A ministry official added that an agency would be set up to manage the bonds and the Bank of Thailand was expected to come up with proposals on the issue by next week.

Thai markets have been roiled this week after the government on Monday ordered a major shakeup of the sector by ordering 10 finance firms facing liquidity problems to boost their capital by a total of 8.25 billion baht ($317 million).
Authorities this week also told banks and finance companies to make extra provisions for sub-standard loans, primarily to the depressed property sector.
